EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains on high alert with a confirmed Israeli elimination of Hamas military chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad in Gaza City, intensifying the conflict there. Simultaneously, reports indicate active US and Israeli preparations for renewed and potentially aggressive military operations against Iran, as diplomatic efforts appear stalled and President Trump issues stark warnings. The precarious ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has been extended, yet cross-border attacks persist, highlighting regional instability.

IRAN
Reports from the New York Times indicate intense US and Israeli preparations for a renewed military campaign against Iran in the coming days or next week, potentially under a new name, with options including aggressive bombing of military targets and infrastructure, or deploying special forces to extract deeply buried enriched uranium. President Trump declared the US is "almost finished" its military work in Iran (75% complete) and threatened to "destroy everything in two days," including bridges and power stations, while asserting Iran's military capabilities (navy, air force) are "destroyed." He also stated a "cleanup" of Iranian leadership might be necessary. Iranian President Pezeshkian thanked Pope Leo for his "moral stance" against US-Israeli aggression and urged international action against "illegal demands." Mohammad Mokhber, an advisor to the Iranian Leader, warned that Iran's restraint is "not permanent." Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that the issue of enriched material with the US is at an "impasse" and that the US war imposed "avoidable economic costs" on Americans. Internal reports indicate the body of Abdolrahim Mousavi, former Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, was found after 30 days under rubble following an alleged US-Israeli attack on the "Leader's residence" in Tehran. Controlled explosions of unexploded ordnance were carried out in Dezful, Shiraz, and Konarak from recent attacks, and a significant oil leak has been observed off Maroo (Shidor) Island in the Persian Gulf following an attack on Lavan oil facilities. Iran's football federation is scheduled to meet with FIFA in Istanbul to discuss the team's safety and participation in the World Cup in the US. Iranian hackers are suspected of penetrating US gas station fuel systems, though no damage was reported.

ISRAEL
Israel confirmed the killing of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the commander of Hamas’s military wing in Gaza City, in an airstrike last night, identifying him as one of the "architects of the October 7 massacre." His wife, daughter, and four aides were also killed in the strike, which involved three fighter jets and 13 bombs on a residential building in the Rimal neighborhood. Defense Minister Israel Katz updated former hostage Liri Albag’s family, who was held by al-Haddad. A senior Israeli official indicated that a "renewal of fighting is approaching," with Israel preparing for "days to weeks of fighting," pending a decision from President Trump within 24 hours. The IDF announced a wave of airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, reporting over 440 targets hit and more than 220 operatives killed in the past week, including weapon depots in Tyre. Hostile aircraft intrusions triggered sirens in the Mount Meron area (drone fell, no injuries) and the Galilee Panhandle/Western Galilee (drones intercepted or fell in open areas, impacts identified in Kiryat Shmona and Metula). A rocket fired by Hezbollah at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon was intercepted. The IDF concluded a snap drill, "Sulfur and Fire," on the Jordanian border, simulating various threats including infiltration and drone attacks, with a 100% reservist turnout in the 96th Division. A closed military zone was imposed on the Rosh Hanikra and Achziv coastal strip starting May 15, 21:20 UTC.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City resulted in the confirmed death of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, commander of Hamas’s military wing, along with his wife, daughter, and four aides. Press TV reported seven people killed, including three women, in Gaza City airstrikes. Civil defense teams were attempting to extinguish fires in a bombed residential building in the Al-Rimal neighborhood. On the occasion of Nakba anniversary, Hamas and Islamic Jihad reaffirmed their commitment to resistance against Israel. In the West Bank and al-Quds, Palestinian worshippers and properties were subjected to aggression, with settlers reportedly torching a mosque and storming the al-Aqsa Mosque compound. An armed Israeli settler was filmed beating a guard dog to death in Attara, north of Ramallah, and settlers also set fire to Palestinian properties in Shuqba, west of Ramallah.

LEBANON
Despite the US announcing a 45-day extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, cross-border hostilities continued. Hezbollah launched multiple drones, rockets, and mortars towards northern Israel, with alarms sounding in areas including Mount Meron, Kiryat Shmona, and Metula. Some drones were intercepted, others exploded in open areas, and some caused impacts. Hezbollah also targeted Israeli troops in southern Lebanon with drones and rockets, and attempted to shoot down an Israeli Air Force drone, which failed. The IDF confirmed extensive airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, including in Tyre and Al-Marwaniya, stating over 440 targets were hit and over 220 operatives killed in the past week. Lebanese sources reported casualties from these Israeli strikes. The Israeli right-wing minister Itamar Ben-Gvir reportedly announced plans for illegal settlements in southern Lebanon and mass displacement of Palestinians. The Lebanese Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, after talks in Washington, criticized "absurd adventures" and a "war not chosen" that led to Israeli occupation of 68 villages, emphasizing the need for a single national decision and army.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The US arrested Mohammed Baqir Saad Daoud al-Saadi, a senior commander in Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah, and charged him with planning at least 18 terror attacks in Europe, the US, and Canada since late February. These attacks, including an alleged plan to bomb a New York synagogue and target Jewish institutions in Los Angeles and Arizona, were reportedly in retaliation for US and Israeli attacks on Iran. Al-Saadi is accused of knowing Qassem Soleimani personally. Ali al-Zaidi officially assumed the role of Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, receiving congratulations from Iranian President Pezeshkian and Russian Prime Minister Mishustin. Pezeshkian vowed Iran's continued support for Iraq. However, political instability is emerging within the Iraqi government, with several factions, including Ammar Youssef, Asadi, Gherawi, and Al-Fayyad, reportedly withdrawing from the Al-Sudani coalition. Israeli forces were reported to have intruded into Syria's Quneitra province, conducting raids on homes.

GULF STATES
The UAE unsuccessfully attempted to persuade Saudi Arabia and Qatar to join a coordinated military campaign against Iran during the recent conflict, with both countries reportedly declining, stating "this is not their war." The UAE is accelerating the construction of a new oil pipeline to Fujairah, aiming to double its export capacity by 2027 and significantly bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Tension was evident at the BRICS Foreign Ministers meeting in Delhi, where Iran and the UAE had differing views on the conflict, preventing a joint statement. Israeli channel i24 reported that Abu Dhabi was "very angry" about the leak of details concerning a planned visit by Netanyahu, perceiving it as a breach of trust driven by Israeli domestic politics. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that the Strait of Hormuz is expected to reopen by summer, but warned that the US military might intervene if Iran continues to disrupt shipping. China criticized a US-Bahraini draft resolution at the UNSC urging Iran to cease attacks in Hormuz, which Russia and China are expected to veto.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Hamas Military Commander Eliminated:** Israeli forces killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the commander of Hamas's military wing and an "architect of the Oct 7 massacre," in a Gaza City airstrike on May 15. His wife, daughter, and four aides were also killed.
2.  **US/Israel Prepare for Renewed Iran War:** The New York Times reported that the US and Israel are making intensive preparations for a potential renewal of military operations against Iran in the coming days, possibly including aggressive bombing or special forces to extract nuclear material.
3.  **Trump's Ultimatum to Iran:** President Trump stated his patience with Iran had run out, threatening to destroy Iranian infrastructure "in two days" and suggesting a "cleanup" of Iranian leadership might be needed. He also rejected Iran's latest nuclear proposal as "unacceptable."
4.  **Lebanon Ceasefire Extended Amid Attacks:** The US announced a 45-day extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, but Hezbollah launched multiple drones, rockets, and mortars into northern Israel, while the IDF conducted extensive airstrikes, hitting over 440 Hezbollah targets and killing over 220 operatives in the past week.
5.  **Arrest of Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah Commander:** Mohammed Baqir Saad Daoud al-Saadi, a senior commander in Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah, was arrested by the US and charged with planning 18 terror attacks in Europe, US, and Canada in retaliation for US/Israeli actions.
6.  **Strait of Hormuz Under Threat:** Iran's Mohammad Mokhber declared the Strait of Hormuz has the capacity of an "atomic bomb" and threatened to bar Israeli ships unless war compensation is paid. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright warned of potential US military intervention if Iran disrupts shipping.
7.  **UAE Diverges on Iran War:** The UAE failed to convince Saudi Arabia and Qatar to join a coordinated military campaign against Iran and is accelerating a pipeline to bypass Hormuz, signaling strategic divergence within the GCC.
8.  **Death of Iranian Chief of Staff:** Ali Mousavi, son of former Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces Abdolrahim Mousavi, claimed his father's body was found after 30 days under rubble following a US-Israeli attack on the "Leader's residence" in Tehran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
**Escalation Risks:** The risk of significant escalation in the Middle East is critically high. President Trump's explicit threats of renewed military action against Iran, coupled with reports of intensive US and Israeli preparations, suggest a potential large-scale conflict. Iran's defiant statements regarding the Strait of Hormuz and its "non-permanent restraint" further heighten this risk.
**Active Flashpoints:** Gaza remains a flashpoint following the elimination of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, with likely retaliation from Hamas. The northern Israel-southern Lebanon border is highly active despite a ceasefire extension, indicating continued cross-border exchanges. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical flashpoint, with Iranian threats to shipping and potential US military intervention.
**Military Posture Changes:** The US and Israel are reportedly preparing for aggressive military options against Iran, including ground operations for nuclear material. The IDF's extensive snap drill on the Jordanian border demonstrates high-level regional readiness. France has deployed its aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Strait of Hormuz to ensure freedom of navigation.
**Red Lines:** US red lines include Iran developing nuclear weapons and disrupting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's red lines include direct military action against its sovereignty and infrastructure. Any perceived violation of these could trigger immediate and widespread conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump returned from China and is expected to decide on renewed military action against Iran within 24 hours. He has threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure and conduct a "cleanup" of Iranian leadership. The US also announced a 45-day extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire and arrested a senior Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah commander for terror plots. Trump discussed the Strait of Hormuz with Xi Jinping, agreeing on the need for it to remain open.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia and Qatar rejected the UAE's push for joint military action against Iran. The UAE is accelerating a pipeline to bypass Hormuz and expressed anger over leaks regarding Netanyahu's visit. Tensions between Iran and the UAE were apparent at the BRICS foreign ministers meeting, preventing a joint statement.
**EU Members:** German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a phone call with Trump, agreeing that Iran must come to the negotiating table, open Hormuz, and not acquire nuclear weapons. France deployed its aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Strait of Hormuz. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez defended his country's non-participation in Eurovision due to Israel's actions, stating "silence is not an option."
**Russia:** President Putin is scheduled to visit China on May 19-20. Russia, along with China, is expected to veto a US-Bahraini draft UNSC resolution on the Strait of Hormuz. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin congratulated Ali al-Zaidi on becoming Iraq's new Prime Minister.
**China:** President Xi Jinping met with President Trump, both agreeing on the importance of an open Strait of Hormuz. China criticized the US-Bahraini resolution on Hormuz, calling its content and timing inappropriate. Chinese media generally summarized Trump's visit as yielding few significant achievements, with a focus on strengthening relations.
**Pakistan:** President Trump cited Pakistan's request as the reason for agreeing to a temporary ceasefire with Iran. Pakistan's Foreign Minister announced the repatriation of Pakistani and Iranian citizens seized on ships by US forces.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions between Sources:** There is an unconfirmed but highly significant claim by Ali Mousavi, son of former Chief of Staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, that his father's body was found after 30 days under rubble following a US-Israeli attack on the "Leader's residence." While other Iranian sources (Shargh, Press TV, Vahid Online) report the death of Abdolrahim Mousavi, the specific target of the attack (Leader's residence) is not corroborated elsewhere and could be a euphemism or a highly sensitive unconfirmed detail. Initial reports from Israeli officials stated "initial indications" of al-Haddad's death before full confirmation.
**Unverified Claims:** President Trump's assertions about Iran's military capabilities being "destroyed" (navy, air force) and specific details about Iran's nuclear material storage ("granite mountain") are strong rhetorical claims not independently verified. Omid Dana's strong predictions of the Islamic Republic's imminent downfall are personal opinions. Naya's channel reports unverified claims of desertions and attempted flag changes within the Iranian military.
**Propaganda Indicators:** Both Israeli and Iranian sources employ strong, often emotional language to frame events. Israeli reports emphasize al-Haddad's role as an "architect of the Oct 7 massacre" to justify his elimination. Iranian sources describe US/Israeli actions as "aggression," "genocide," and "colonialism," focusing on civilian casualties and perceived moral decay of the West. Trump's rhetoric (e.g., "group of madmen," "cleanup") serves as a strong signal to domestic and international audiences.
**Reporting Gaps:** Specific details regarding the ongoing Israel-Lebanon ceasefire negotiations are limited, beyond the extension announcement and general positive remarks from the Israeli side contrasted with Lebanese criticism. The exact number and identities of casualties from Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, beyond general Lebanese claims, are not provided. The full impact and details of alleged Iranian cyberattacks on US gas stations remain unclear.
